question: How hoi3_tfh.exe hosts Lua: its states, libraries, loaders, luabind, the new-game call of AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation, == on API objects, and the x87 precision.

addresses.name: GetThreadLuaState
addresses.comment:
**A Lua state per thread, and every AI Lua call in the image goes through it.** Reads the TLS array at `fs:[0x2C]`, and on a thread's first use takes `EnterCriticalSection(0x1B15418)`, news 4 bytes, calls `luaL_newstate` (0xD2B478) and `luaL_openlibs` (0xD2B46C), and runs `script/autoexec.lua` (0x15EC700). Returns a pointer to the slot, so callers do `mov edi, [eax]` to get the lua_State. That the AI needs a per-thread state is the other half of the evidence that it runs on TBB workers.

**The whole of a state's birth, read 2026-10-12 (VAs)**, under the lock: `operator new(4)`, `luaL_newstate`, `luaL_openlibs` - **all eight standard libraries**, the stock 5.1.4 table base/package/table/io/os/string/math/debug, nothing removed afterwards - then **SetupAI(L)** (0x8EAE30, which opens luabind with `luabind::open` 0xB7EFD0 and registers the whole API), then **Lua_InstallPhysfsLoader** (0x8F1180: `table.insert(package.loaders, 2, <PhysicsFS searcher>)`), then **RunLuaFile("script/autoexec.lua", slot, "")** (0xAA8290, through PhysicsFS, so the mod's copy, else tfh's, else the base game's), and last **RegisterThreadLuaStateSlot** (0x901DA0), which appends the slot to the vector at 0x1B153D8 that the console's reload command walks. The slot is the exe's own `__declspec(thread)` variable at TLS index 0 + 4, so **one state per OS thread**, made on that thread's first call and never closed (`lua_close` is not imported). 21 call sites: LoadDefines - which is why the main thread's state exists before any game, and why the engine's defines come out of it - SetUpCountryForNewGame twice, the five AI ministers, the six DiploScore bridges, the hourly AI trade, the daily leadership pass and the production screen's trade list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-luahost.md.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x8EACA0-0x8EADE1 from the unpatched copy: every call named above is a direct call in that order, the strings are literals, the lock is EnterCriticalSection/LeaveCriticalSection on 0x1B15418. luaL_newstate and luaL_openlibs each have exactly one call site in the image (import scan over all 56 lua51.dll IAT slots). The library table luaL_openlibs walks was read out of lua5.1.dll.preBlackICE at 0x10021230: eight entries then a null. Wrong if a second luaL_newstate site existed - the scan finds call [iat], mov reg,[iat] and jmp-thunks, and finds the one known site.
addresses.revises: The comment said the state runs autoexec; it now says everything done to a new state, in order, the per-thread slot, and who asks. Name and signature unchanged; no_signature added as null, which the entry lacked.

addresses.name: PrepareLuaCall_AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl PrepareLuaCall_AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation(void* call@ESI, void* luaState@EDI, CCountry** country@stack:4, CCountryTag* target@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: **luabind 0.9's `call_function<int>(L, "AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation", country, tag)` up to the call**: `lua_pushstring` the name (0x15C0F10) and `lua_gettable(L, LUA_GLOBALSINDEX)` on the state in EDI, then it fills the proxy_function_caller in ESI: +0 the state, +4 = 1 (the stack slots the proxy owns: the function), **+8 = 0xB7E9D0, `luabind::detail::pcall`** - the function the proxy calls with, not an argument pusher, as this said until 2026-10-12 - +0xC and +0x10 the addresses of the two arguments (a `CCountry*` and a `CCountryTag`), +0x14 = 0, the `called` flag. Returns ESI. The caller converts it with LuaCallProxy_CountryTag_CallInt (0x50D2F0) and destroys it with LuaCallProxy_CountryTag_Release (0x50D260). 0x5100D0 to the bare `ret` at 0x510111 (VAs). One caller, SetUpCountryForNewGame at 0x4D71C5.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x5100D0-0x510111: the five stores, the name literal, the two imports. 0xB7E9D0 read: it fetches the luabind pcall callback (0x174C67C), inserts it as the error handler when set, calls lua_pcall(L, nargs, nresults, handler) through the thunk and removes the handler - which is luabind::detail::pcall line for line. 0x50D2F0 calls [proxy+8] with (L, 2, 1). Wrong if +8 were called with anything but (L, nargs, nresults).
addresses.revises: +8 was described as 'the argument pusher'; it is luabind::detail::pcall. The argument pusher is 0x511830, called separately. +0x14 is the called flag. Raised to confirmed.

addresses.name: SetUpCountryForNewGame
addresses.comment:
**What a country starts a new game with**: the effects of the decisions its history says it has taken, its war exhaustion, its stockpile, its diplomatic influence, **its relation with every other country and its first spy allocation**, and its manpower. One stack argument, `ret 4` at 0x4D757A. One caller, 0x65B4F2 in CInGameIdler::Enter, inside the block that gamestate->loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) == 0 guards, so it never runs on a load. **The function before it ends `ret 4` at 0x4D622D with no padding** - a walk back from inside this one answers 0x4D59D0, which is what fieldchain.py prints (trap 2). (Addresses in this comment are VAs.)

**The decisions** (VA 0x4D6342-0x4D668A, read 2026-10-12): after UpdateIC(country, 0) at 0x4D633D it builds a CEventScope whose country is this one (CCountry +0xCA4), FROM `---`, province 0, and **random_state, its copy and seed all 0**, and walks the country's **taken list** (+0x128, next at node +0x20) - the names its history's `decision = <name>` entries put there, less any `remove_decision`, through CCountryDecisionChange::Apply. Each name is looked up **in the political table first and then the diplomatic** (the reverse of CExecuteDecisionCommand's order); not found, it logs `<TAG> has unknown decision '<name>'` under country.cpp; found, **its effect runs** - CEffect::Execute (slot 11) with (scope, 0) at 0x4D6658. Neither `potential` nor `allow` is asked, no message is raised and no history entry is filed. The scope's random state is never reset between decisions, so each draws on where the one before left it.

Read from 0x4D69DF to 0x4D7108 and from 0x4D7346 to the end. Months are calendar months, year * 12 + month off the tick. At war (at_war, +0xACC): began = the earliest 0xA51D20(war) over the active wars (gamestate +0xC00) the country is an attacker or defender in, and war_exhaustion (+0xAD0) = min(months since * 0.05, 10). Otherwise war_exhaustion = max(3 - months since the latest 0xA51F40(war) over previous_war (+0xC20) * 0.05, 0). Then **days = 30 + 5 * max(12 - months at war, 2)** - 90 at peace, five fewer a month of war, never under 40 - and amount = MaxIC (+0x60C) * days, **held to 1000 for a subject (isSubject, +0xF34)**. Into the acting capital's pool, each an `add`: crude oil and metal `amount`, energy twice it, rare materials half; money, **only when the pool has none**, amount * IC_TO_MONEY * 0.05; supplies and fuel, `days` times the sum of CUnit::SupplyConsumption and CUnit::FuelConsumption over the country's units (+0xBAC). Then **diplo_influence (+0xA88) = MaxIC / 5 in whole points**. The 0.05 is g_OneTwentieth.

**The dates** (0x4D668A loop, read 2026-10-12): for every country of the database, a pair whose war_seen_tick (`last_war`, +0x54) is later than now is put back to g_NullDate.

**The relations** (0x4D710E..0x4D733F, read 2026-10-12, FINDINGS-diplostate.md): skipped whole for REB and for a country that owns no province (+0xCF8). Otherwise for every country B of the database in order, REB and itself included: value = 25; when B is not REB and owns a province, value = the Lua global **`AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation(country, B)`** (script/ai_country.lua; the call is built by PrepareLuaCall_AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation, 0x5100D0, and run by 0x50D2F0 for an integer - see the Lua paragraph below), whole points. Then, **only when `diplomacy[B]->relation (+0x38)` is exactly 0**, it becomes clamp(value * 1000, -200000, 200000) with `changed (+0x59) = 1` - **this country's side only**. So a relation the history set is kept, a computed 0 is written as 0, and an existing country is left with 25 towards REB and towards every country that does not exist. In the same loop, for a B that exists and is not REB, the first spy allocation - entry +0 of the 0xF8-byte record B in the array at espionage (+0x1160) - is 1000 * score clamped to [0, g_MaxSpyLevel], score = [value < -100] + [value < 0] + neighbours[B] (+0xF58) + [same continent (+0x368 of each acting capital)] + 2 * [both factions valid and different] + [ruling_ideology (+0x1140) differs] + 2 * [diplomacy[B]->war] - 2 * [diplomacy[B]->alliance] + 3 * [B is this country], **halved toward zero when CCountry::IsMajor (0x4F8AB0) says no**. Against the start save the non-self entries of Germany's row agree; the self entries are 1 higher for the seven majors than this gives, which was not explained.

**The tail is the manpower.** ReapplyAllTechnologies (0x4D7346), **the Lua global `Laws(country)`** (0x4D734B-0x4D7375, below), RebuildStaticModifiers (0x4D7380), UpdateMaxManpower (0x4D7386), and then **manpower (+0xBCC) = max_manpower (+0xBD0)**, a `mov` - so whatever `manpower` a country's history file gave is overwritten. If it owns a province (the count at +0xCF8 above 0) and is at war, it then loses year * (1000 + months at war * g_StartingManpowerLostPerMonthAtWar / 1000) / 1000, where year = max_manpower * 1000 / MAX_MANPOWER and the months are the same thousandths the war exhaustion used; floored at 0. After that it sets the date at +0xAB0 to today's when it holds one before year 3, and calls 0x4F06D0 and 0x4F72F0.

Not read: VA 0x4D6230-0x4D6342 (a month count from the last election at +0xAB0, then UpdateIC(country, 0) at 0x4D633D).

**The two Lua calls** (read 2026-10-12, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-luahost.md; VAs). Both take the main thread's state from GetThreadLuaState and sit in try blocks whose only handler is `catch (luabind::error&)` (FuncInfo 0x16C98D8: states 22-23 handler 0x4D7324, state 25 handler 0x4D73CF), and each handler only calls ReportLuaError (0xAA8050, `LUA Error:` in the log) and resumes after the call. **The relation**: [ebp-0x20] is set to 25 at 0x4D7173 before the call and is the result only if the call returns, so **a missing function or a Lua error leaves 25**; the result is `lua_tointeger` of a value that must be a number - `fld`/`fistp` in the Lua DLL, so **rounded to nearest, ties to even**, not truncated - and anything else (nil, a string, a boolean) throws `luabind::cast_failed`, which is **not** a `luabind::error` (its ThrowInfo 0x164B1E4 lists only cast_failed and std::exception) and so escapes this function and CInGameIdler::Enter, which has no try block at all. The country goes in as a `CCountry*` (pushed as a pointer instance, nil if null) and B as a **fresh copy of its CCountryTag**. **`Laws(country)`**: built by PrepareLuaCall_Laws (0x510120) and made by LuaCallProxy_Country_CallVoid (0x50D3F0) with one argument and no result, **for every country this function runs for, with no test of who plays it** - so `script/ai_politics_minister.lua`'s `Laws(minister)` runs with the CCountry where it expects a minister, which works because CCountry also has GetCountryTag, and posts a CChangeLawCommand for each law group it wants moved. That is how the script runs before the first hour (the open question in FINDINGS-unitstart.md).
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4D7100-0x4D73E9 from the unpatched copy. The Laws call: GetThreadLuaState at 0x4D734B, PrepareLuaCall_Laws at 0x4D7368 pushes the literal 'Laws' (0x15C0F34) and stores [ebp+8] (the country) as the one argument, 0x50D3F0 calls [proxy+8] with (L, 1, 0); no branch between ReapplyAllTechnologies and it. The handlers' types were read from the FuncInfo's HandlerType entries, both '.?AVerror@luabind@@'. Wrong if another catch covered state 23 - the try map has two entries and both were printed.
addresses.revises: The tail was described as ReapplyAllTechnologies then RebuildStaticModifiers; between them is a second Lua call, Laws(country), which the comment did not mention. Adds what the relation call does on an error, how its result is rounded, and how both arguments are pushed. Everything else is the recorded text unchanged.

addresses.name: LuaCallProxy_CountryTag_CallInt
addresses.comment: luabind 0.9's `proxy_function_caller<int, (CCountry*, CCountryTag)>::operator int()` - the call itself. Sets `called` (+0x14), notes lua_gettop, pushes the two arguments (LuaPushArgs_CountryAndTag, 0x511830), calls `[proxy+8]` (luabind::detail::pcall) with (L, 2, 1) and **throws `luabind::error(L)`** (vftable 0x15C1CF0, ThrowInfo 0x164B21C) when that answers non-zero, the message left on the stack. Then **`lua_type(L, -1)` must be 3, a number**, or it throws `luabind::cast_failed` (vftable 0x15BB2F0, ThrowInfo 0x164B1E4, type_info of int at 0x17131F0) - a numeric string is refused, not coerced. The answer is `lua_tointeger(L, -1)`, which in this lua5.1.dll is `fld qword; fistp dword` and so rounds to nearest, ties to even, under the thread's x87 rounding mode; the stack is then cut back. One caller, SetUpCountryForNewGame at 0x4D71D2. `ret 4` at 0x50D3E9 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x50D2F0-0x50D3E9 whole; the throw types are from the ThrowInfos' catchable-type arrays, the rounding from lua5.1.dll.preBlackICE's lua_tointeger (0x100015F0: fld/fistp, no _ftol). Wrong if lua_tointeger were the magic-number variant - it is not, the bytes are fistp.

addresses.name: LuaCallProxy_CountryTag_Release
addresses.comment: The same proxy's destructor: if `called` (+0x14) is still clear it makes the call now, with (L, 2, 0) and no result, throwing `luabind::error` on failure; then it cuts the stack back. After LuaCallProxy_CountryTag_CallInt it does nothing but that. Proxy in ESI, bare `ret` at 0x50D2E3 (VAs). One caller, 0x4D71DE.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; the shape is LuaEvaluateDecision_Release's (rva 0x49E5B0) with a 2-argument tuple. Wrong if the flag tested were not the one CallInt sets - both are +0x14.

addresses.name: LuaCallProxy_Country_CallVoid
addresses.comment: The destructor of luabind's one-argument `proxy_function_caller<void, (CCountry*)>`, which **is where a void call_function is made**: if `called` (+0x10) is clear it sets it, pushes the argument (LuaPushArgs_Country, 0x5118A0), calls `[proxy+8]` with (L, 1, 0) and throws `luabind::error` on a non-zero answer, then cuts the stack back. Used for `Laws(country)`. Proxy in ESI, bare `ret` at 0x50D469 (VAs). One caller, SetUpCountryForNewGame at 0x4D7370.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole. Wrong if the call were made elsewhere - the only call through [proxy+8] for this proxy is here, and PrepareLuaCall_Laws leaves +0x10 at 0.

addresses.name: PrepareLuaCall_Laws
addresses.signature: void* __cdecl PrepareLuaCall_Laws(void* call@ESI, lua_State* L@EDI, CCountry** country@stack:4) @EAX
addresses.comment: luabind's `call_function<void>(L, "Laws", country)` up to the call: pushes 'Laws' (0x15C0F34), `lua_gettable(L, LUA_GLOBALSINDEX)`, and fills the proxy in ESI - +0 the state, +4 = 1, +8 = luabind::detail::pcall (0xB7E9D0), +0xC the argument's address, +0x10 = 0 (called). Returns ESI. The global is `Laws(minister)` of script/ai_politics_minister.lua, here handed a CCountry. 0x510120 to the bare `ret` at 0x51015B (VAs). One caller, SetUpCountryForNewGame at 0x4D7368.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole: the literal and the four stores. Wrong if the name were not pushed from here - 0x15C0F34 has this one reference.

addresses.name: LuaPushArgs_CountryAndTag
addresses.comment: Pushes a luabind argument tuple of (CCountry*, CCountryTag). The first: **nil when the pointer is null**; otherwise `__RTDynamicCast` to `luabind::wrap_base` (type descriptors 0x17147B8 CCountry, 0x17147E8 wrap_base) - a Lua-derived object would push its existing Lua self (0xB7C320) - and failing that a new pointer instance (0x514550), **no copy, no cache**. The second through LuaPush_CCountryTagByValue (0x5137C0), **a copy**. Bare `ret` at 0x51187E and 0x51189B (VAs). Two callers, the int and void proxies of this tuple.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole. Wrong if the null test were absent - it is the first branch, to lua_pushnil.

addresses.name: LuaPushArgs_Country
addresses.comment: The one-argument form of LuaPushArgs_CountryAndTag: the CCountry* as nil when null, a wrap_base's own Lua object (0xB7C320) when the dynamic cast succeeds, or a new pointer instance (0x514550). Bare `ret` at 0x5118B4, 0x5118D9 and 0x5118E6 (VAs). One caller, LuaCallProxy_Country_CallVoid.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole, 0x5118A0-0x5118E6; the same three arms as 0x511830's first argument.

addresses.name: LuaPush_CCountryTagByValue
addresses.comment: **A CCountryTag goes to Lua by value**: `operator new(8)`, the tag's two dwords copied in, and the copy handed to luabind's instance maker (0x5157B0) in an auto_ptr - the `pointer_holder<auto_ptr<CCountryTag>>` of the RTTI - so Lua owns a fresh tag and a script that keeps it holds no reference into the engine. 25 callers. Bare `ret` at 0x51383A (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; callers clean 8 bytes (add esp, 8 at 0x511877). Wrong if the 8 bytes were not copied - they are, mov [eax],esi / mov [eax+4],edi from the source.

addresses.name: Lua_PhysfsChunkReader
addresses.signature: const char* __cdecl Lua_PhysfsChunkReader(lua_State* L, void* data, unsigned int* size)
addresses.comment: The `lua_Reader` Lua_LoadPhysfsChunk hands lua_load: `data` is a 0x200-byte buffer with the PHYSFS_File* at +0x200; reads up to 0x200 bytes with PHYSFS_read (0xB838E0), stores the count through `size` and returns the buffer; a -1 count raises `error reading file: %s` with PHYSFS_getLastError. Bare `ret` (VAs 0x8F0F5C, 0x8F0F67).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; PHYSFS_read and PHYSFS_getLastError are the exe's own exports at those addresses. Wrong if the buffer size differed - 0x200 is the immediate and the handle offset.

addresses.name: Lua_LoadPhysfsChunk
addresses.signature: int __cdecl Lua_LoadPhysfsChunk(const char* path@ESI, lua_State* L@EDI) @EAX
addresses.comment: Opens `path` with PHYSFS_openRead (0xB85140) - `couldn't open file: '%s'` through luaL_error if it cannot - and `lua_load`s it with Lua_PhysfsChunkReader and **the bare path as the chunk name** (no '@', so messages read `[string "script/x.lua"]:N:`); a load error is re-raised with lua_error. Closes the file and returns 1, the loaded chunk on the stack. Bare `ret` at 0x8F0FD9 and two earlier error exits (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; the push order before lua_load puts ESI in the chunkname slot.

addresses.name: Lua_PhysfsLoader
addresses.comment: **The package.loaders searcher the engine adds, at position 2** - before Lua's own path and C searchers, so `require` never reaches `package.path` for a file the game's file system has. For `require(name)` it asks PHYSFS_exists (FileExists, 0xB84A20) of `script/<name>.lua`, then `script/country/<name>.lua`, then `common/<name>.lua`, each over the whole PhysicsFS search path (mod, tfh, base), and loads the first that exists with Lua_LoadPhysfsChunk; when none does it pushes `\n\tno physfs file '%s'` (the last tried) for require's message. Returns 1. So `require('defines')` is common/defines.lua and `require('GER')` script/country/GER.lua. Bare `ret` at 0x8F117C (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; the three prefixes and '.lua' are literals, the order is the code's. Wrong if it were not in package.loaders - Lua_InstallPhysfsLoader puts this address there.

addresses.name: Lua_InstallPhysfsLoader
addresses.comment: `table.insert(package.loaders, 2, Lua_PhysfsLoader)`, done by fetching table.insert and package.loaders, pushing 2.0 (the double at 0x160A360) and a closure of 0x8F0FE0, and lua_call(3, 0). Run once per new state, after SetupAI and before autoexec. State in ESI, bare `ret` at 0x8F1217 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole and the stack effect followed push by push; 0x160A360 reads 2.0.

addresses.name: RunLuaFile
addresses.signature: int __fastcall RunLuaFile(Hoi3CString* path@ECX, lua_State** state@stack:4, Hoi3CString* function@stack:8) @EAX
addresses.comment: Reads a whole file through the game's PhysicsFS file object (open 0xA6C1B0, PHYSFS_fileLength 0xB839C0, read 0xA6C880 - PHYSFS_read), `luaL_loadbuffer(L, buf, size, path)` - **chunk name the bare path** - and `lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0)`, **no message handler**. If both succeed and `function` is not empty, CallLuaGlobal(function). Any non-zero answer goes to ReportLuaError. Returns that answer. GetThreadLuaState passes `script/autoexec.lua` and an empty function; the console reload command (0x43B1D0) runs a named file in every registered state. `ret 8` at 0xAA83B8 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; ECX is used as a std::string (+0x14 capacity test) and the two stack arguments are read at [ebp+8] and [ebp+0xC]. Wrong if the pcall had a handler - its fourth argument is the zero in EAX.

addresses.name: CallLuaGlobal
addresses.comment: `lua_getfield(L, LUA_GLOBALSINDEX, name)` and `lua_pcall(L, 0, 0, 0)`; a failure goes to ReportLuaError. Returns the pcall's answer. Bare `ret` at 0xAA83FD (VAs). One caller, RunLuaFile.
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole.

addresses.name: ReportLuaError
addresses.comment: Where every Lua failure in the image ends: if the top of the stack is a string it is copied and popped, a log record is made under `luainterface.cpp` with `\nLUA Error: ` and the message (plus ` - no script source to reload` when its look up the call stack, 0xAA7C30, finds no source). Nothing is shown to the player and nothing is retried. 21 callers - every engine Lua call site's `catch (luabind::error&)` handler and RunLuaFile/CallLuaGlobal. Bare `ret` at 0xAA8283 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded to the ret; the literals and LogRecord::Make/FlushAndDestruct are direct. The 21 callers were attributed by owner and are all Lua call sites.

addresses.name: RegisterThreadLuaStateSlot
addresses.comment: `push_back` of a thread's state slot onto the vector at 0x1B153D8 (begin, end +4, capacity +8), growing it through 0x903880. Called once, at the end of GetThreadLuaState's first-use path. Bare `ret` at 0x901DEA and 0x901E13 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; it handles the aliasing case of push_back(v[i]).

addresses.name: luabind::open
addresses.comment: luabind 0.9's `open`: refuses a non-main lua_State (`luabind::open() must be called with the main thread lua_State*`), makes the registry entries `__luabind_classes`, `__luabind_class_id_map`, `__luabind_cast_graph` and `__luabind_class_map`, and **sets the globals `class`, `property` and `super`** - the only globals this image adds besides the registered API. Called once, first thing in SetupAI. Bare `ret` at 0xB7F270 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; the strings are the luabind 0.9 set (0.8 has no cast graph or class id map).

addresses.name: luabind::detail::push_instance_metatable
addresses.comment: Builds **the one metatable every luabind instance shares**: `__luabind_class` = true, [1] and `__index` = get_instance_value (0xB7E5C0), `__gc` (0xB7E840), `__newindex` (0xB7E480), and for each of the 13 operator names at 0x16F500C (`__add` ... `__eq` ... `__len`) a closure of dispatch_operator over (name, is-unary) - unary for `__unm` and `__len`. Because the metatable is shared, Lua 5.1 finds the same `__eq` on any two luabind objects. Bare `ret` at 0xB7E9C4 (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; the name table was read entry by entry.

addresses.name: luabind::detail::dispatch_operator
addresses.comment: luabind 0.9.1's operator dispatcher: for operand 1 then 2, if it is a luabind instance (userdata whose metatable's [1] is get_instance_value), `lua_gettable` the operator's name on it - which looks in its class - and if that is not nil, `lua_call` it with the operands and return 1 result. **No operand with the operator: `No such operator defined`**, a Lua error. Bare `ret` at 0xB7E788 and 0xB7E7DA (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole against the 0.9.1 source shape; the error literal is 0x159FD38.

addresses.name: luabind::detail::pcall
addresses.signature: int __cdecl luabind::detail::pcall(lua_State* L, int nargs, int nresults)
addresses.comment: luabind's pcall: if the pcall callback (0x174C67C) is set it is pushed under the function as the message handler; `lua_pcall(L, nargs, nresults, handler)`; the handler removed. **The callback is never set in this image** - 0x174C67C has one reference, the read at 0xB81C20 - so every engine call runs with no handler and no traceback. Bare `ret` at 0xB7EA2C (VAs).
addresses.evidence: Decoded whole; findValue(0x174C67C) over .text answers the one read.

addresses.name: CGovernment::luabind_opeq

addresses.name: GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice
addresses.no_signature: Not read to its end; its arguments - the settings object among them - were not established.
addresses.comment: graphicssettings.cpp's adapter and device check (`Graphic Adapters: `, `Using Adapter [`, multi-sampling). **Creates a test device with D3DCREATE_HARDWARE_VERTEXPROCESSING (0x40)** (0xAA47B8) and, failing that, **D3DCREATE_SOFTWARE_VERTEXPROCESSING (0x20)** (0xAA49D0), and writes whichever worked into the settings' behaviour flags (+0x1C, at 0xAA48BD and 0xAA4AD5) - never `D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE` (0x2). Calls Direct3DCreate9 at 0xAA3EEC (VAs).

addresses.name: CGraphics_CreateDevice
addresses.comment: **The device the game draws with is created without `D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE`.** CGraphics::CGraphics calls `IDirect3D9::CreateDevice` (vtable +0x40 on the object at CGraphics +0x60) at four places, VAs: 0xA6E960 (adapter 1, HAL, flags 0x40), 0xA6EA1F (the `PerfHUD` adapter, REF, 0x40), **0xA6EAE9 (the ordinary path: HAL, flags = settings +0x1C)** and 0xA6ECE8 (the retry at default refresh after Sleep(100), flags = settings +0x1C). The settings flags are 0x40 or 0x20 as GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice wrote them. So Direct3D 9 puts the creating thread's x87 unit into **24-bit precision, round to nearest**.
addresses.evidence: Each call's pushes read: the fifth argument is an immediate 0x40 or a load of [settings+0x1C]. That settings +0x1C is only ever 0x40 or 0x20 rests on the two stores found in the detector (inferred). Wrong if another IDirect3D9 existed - Direct3DCreate9 has two call sites, and both were followed.
